messages:
pagerduty: 🔔 Pager duty: P0 - latency spike + errors on hosted inference (kv-cache blowup). Pager ID: PD-8421. Trigger: kv-cache memory > 95% and continuous-batcher error rate > 10%. thread created at 1799991111

alex chu: I'm on it. seeing big jump in outstanding batch size and rapid kv-cache evictions.

maya rao: Paging in. Any error logs or stack traces?

alex chu: logs: `batcher: broke batch at seq=0 len=1 reason=tool_call_structured` repeated. also `kv_cache: key_size=~2.1MB key_count=4.2M mem=96%`

eva-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-kvcache-toolcall. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-batch

sam t: Quick context — this started ~03:05 UTC after the rollout of model-v2-toolcall (canary). Canary has structured function output templates enabled by default.

maya rao: Repro note: when function responses contain nested arrays/objects with long keys, the batcher treats them as unique prefixes and avoids prefix coalescing, causing many tiny batches and unique cache keys.

sre-lead: Customer-facing impact?

alex chu: Preliminary: 7% of hosted requests in EU/NA saw 5-15s tail latency and ~2% 5xxs (model errors). Some long-running requests hit memlimit and returned 429s.

customer-success: We already have two tickets from enterprise customers complaining about degraded perf. One flagged production traffic with SLA warnings.

maya rao: Mitigation plan (in order):
1) revert canary model -> model-v2-no-toolcall (rollback canary config).
2) temporarily disable structured output postprocessing at the batch layer (patch to batcher to strip tool metadata from cache key).
3) increase kv-cache evict threshold and add short TTL for new keys.
4) scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes to relieve pressure.

alex chu: I'm applying (1) now. calling the deployment bot: `@deploy-bot rollback hosted/model-v2-toolcall --to model-v2-20260303 --env prod`

eva-bot: Deploy request received. Canary rollback initiated.

sam t: While rollback runs, I'm prepping a hotfix to batcher to stop using full serialized function output as cache key. Patch: only use prompt+model+tool_name+normalized_signature. Code snippet:```json
{"cache_key_components": ["prompt_hash","model","tool_name","signature_hash"]}```

maya rao: Good. Also add a sanitizer that collapses long object keys into a stable token (hash) so keys don't blow up.

alex chu: Metrics: after rollback start, continuous-batcher error rate dropped from 12% -> 4% in 3 min; kv-cache mem usage still climbing (evictions ongoing).

sre-lead: OK good progress. Prioritize (2) next. If hotfix takes >15m, we may need to evict lowest-priority namespaces manually.

sam t: Hotfix build passing unit tests, pushing to staging for smoke. `build/1258`

maya rao: I'll open a temporary policy to reject requests that contain function outputs >512KB at the ingress; that should prevent new pathological keys while patch rolls out.

alex chu: Ingress policy applied (rate limit + size reject) to hosted-prod. New large requests now respond 413.

customer-success: Noting an update to affected customers — telling them we rolled back canary and are applying hotfix. No data leak, just latency.

eva-bot: Rollback completed at 1799991605. Canary removed from 10% traffic.

alex chu: After rollback: 5xxs dropped to baseline, request p95 latency still elevated ~20% vs normal but trending down.

sam t: Hotfix deployed to prod at 1799992400 (hotfix build 1258). Patch: batcher now normalizes function output sections before computing cache key; added unit + integration tests.

maya rao: After hotfix: continuous-batcher errors down to 0.8%, kv-cache mem usage slowly falling (eviction rate normalized).

sre-lead: Scale down plan? Keep +2 nodes for 1 hour post-incident, then autoscale decisions.

alex chu: Agree. I'll keep nodes up for 1h and monitor.

customer-success: Customers informed; one enterprise asked for postmortem and SLA credit assessment.

maya rao: Impact summary for postmortem: root cause = structured function outputs introduced by model-v2-toolcall created highly variable serialized outputs used as cache keys -> prevented prefix coalescing and exploded keyspace -> memory pressure -> evictions & tail latency. Contributing factors: canary rollout to 10% + lack of key normalization in batcher + no ingress cap on function output size.

sam t: Follow-ups (action items):
- Normalize cache key construction globally (PR 4321).
- Add quota for function output size at ingress + client SDK warnings.
- Canary more conservatively for features that change serialization shape.
- Add metric: unique_cache_keys_per_min per model+tool to detect blowups earlier.
- Runbook update: add explicit step for tool/function calling regressions.

sre-lead: Assign owners: PR 4321 -> sam t, ingress quota -> maya, metrics -> alex. Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow.

alex chu: Handoff for next oncall (1799994000): monitor kv_cache.mem_percent, continuous_batcher.error_rate, hosted p95, and customer ticket queue. Notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-03-kvcache-toolcall

eva-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-kvcache-toolcall resolved (status: mitigated). Total duration: ~48m.

maya rao: marking P0 -> resolved, moving to postmortem. thanks team :thumbsup:

sam t: I'll draft the technical section of the postmortem and push to the doc in ~1h.

alex chu: Closing monitoring loop. Will follow up if anything regresses.

customer-success: Will coordinate with legal/partner success on SLA credit requests.

sre-lead: Great work. We're keeping this one high priority for the follow-up items.

(reacts: :wave: :heavy_check_mark: on several messages)
